textBlocks.label: Supertouch Kindness Foundation (SKF) began its journey in 2020, rooted
textBlocks.text: Supertouch Kindness Foundation (SKF) began its journey in 2020, rooted in the heart of Maiduguri, Borno State, at a time when communities were overwhelmed by conflict, displacement, and vulnerability. Our early work centered around mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), gender-based violence (GBV) prevention, and access to sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services. We started small — organizing awareness campaigns, distributing dignity kits, and facilitating referrals for GBV survivors in communities like Mairi, Kaleri, and Rann. Our belief was simple: acts of kindness, driven by compassion, can restore dignity and transform lives.

textBlocks.label: Today, our impact has expanded across six states — Borno, Adamawa, Yob
textBlocks.text: Today, our impact has expanded across six states — Borno, Adamawa, Yobe, Taraba, Plateau, and Sokoto — with direct interventions reaching over 34,000 individuals. We’ve empowered women and girls with disabilities to advocate for their rights, trained community-based action teams (COMBATs) to respond to GBV cases, and led capacity-building sessions for service providers, data enumerators, and sign language interpreters. Through collaborative efforts with partners like UNFPA, AUN, RHHF, and CRUDAN, we now lead inclusive humanitarian work that integrates disability rights, youth empowerment, peacebuilding, and community resilience. At SKF, our work is not just about delivering aid — it’s about co-creating sustainable change with the people we serve.

textBlocks.label: At Supertouch Kindness Foundation, our work is guided by compassion, i
textBlocks.text: At Supertouch Kindness Foundation, our work is guided by compassion, inclusion, and the urgent needs of the communities we serve. From our beginnings in Maiduguri to our expansion across North-East Nigeria, we remain committed to empowering vulnerable populations through integrated, people-first solutions.
